name: Disaster Event
description: Schedules, telegraphs, and resolves city-scale disaster events — fires, floods, meteor strikes, or any configured calamity — as a three-phase state machine: warning, active, aftermath. The warning phase exists because a disaster with no telegraph is a coin flip, not a challenge; players must get a window to respond or evacuate before damage begins. Damage itself is not applied here: this component marks affected cells and emits, and the actual destruction, cost, and hazard behavior belong to the systems that own those facts — world.hazard_volume applies ongoing area effects, housing and world structures decide what breaks, and economy.currency decides what repairs cost. Disasters can be random (seeded, so replays and daily cities stay deterministic), scripted, or player-invoked for the sandbox mayor who just wants to watch the world burn.

inputs.name: disasterTable
inputs.description: Disaster definitions: id, footprint shape and size, warning duration, active duration, and intensity scaling. Data-driven so 'alien invasion' and 'kitchen fire' share one state machine.

inputs.name: randomDisastersEnabled
inputs.description: Master switch for ambient disasters. Many players consider random disasters a betrayal of their city; the toggle is a genre expectation, not an option.

inputs.name: randomIntervalMinutes
inputs.description: In-game minute range between ambient disasters, drawn from a seeded RNG. The wide band keeps disasters surprising without clustering.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.description: Seed for disaster scheduling. Deterministic scheduling lets a shared-seed city challenge be fair across players.

outputs.name: activeDisaster
outputs.description: The current disaster with phase, footprint cells, and remaining duration; null when the city is at peace.

outputs.name: disasterHistory
outputs.description: Resolved disasters with cells affected and duration, for post-mortem reports and achievement checks.
